Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.implicit

Class DeviceVerificationRequestGuard

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.implicit.DeviceVerificationRequestGuard
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AuthenticationConverter
public class DeviceVerificationRequestGuard extends Object implements org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AuthenticationConverter
Guards the device verification endpoint. It is installed first among the converters of the endpoint and never converts anything: it either lets the request go on (returning null) or refuses it. Every request that carries a user code (the code typed on the verification page, a link that carries it, and the consent decision) is counted against the limit on the attempts, and the multi-factor policy of the account and of the client must be satisfied, as the authorization endpoint requires before it issues a code: a user who owes a second factor is sent to the second-factor page and resumes afterwards. The framework's own MFA customizer covers only /oauth2/authorize.

The client is the one the device authorization stored for the user code was issued to, because the code typed on the page (or carried by the link) is the only thing the request names: so a client that requires multi-factor authentication is enforced even when it skips the consent page. Only when no authorization holds the code (an unknown or expired one, which the endpoint refuses anyway) is the client_id of the consent decision used.
